correctness.summary: For any conjugation J and distinct unit phases, direct conjugate-linear algebra gives complementary orthogonal idempotents P1,P2 with lambda1 P1+lambda2 P2=J. Restriction of alpha P1+beta P2 to a fixed complex line of J proves that it is isometric exactly when alpha=beta or alpha/beta=lambda1/lambda2. The C^1[0,1] specialization with pointwise conjugation, lambda1=1 and lambda2=i is therefore a generalized bi-circular family with nonzero phase sum that is not bi-circular.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The claim is limited to identifying and formalizing this contradiction to arXiv:2609.18967v1 and its exact phase locus. Older work already contains non-reflection generalized bi-circular examples, and a 2019 corrigendum fixed an omitted case in a related C^1 classification; those are treated as prior art. No public correction/comment to the current v1 stating this specific conjugation counterexample was located. The full 2019 corrigendum was not inspected, so novelty of the mechanism remains qualified.

value.summary: The construction directly falsifies a dichotomy stated in the abstract of a current functional-analysis preprint and its Theorem 3.4. The general conjugation lemma shows a reusable structural failure mechanism rather than an isolated example, and the phase-locus theorem pinpoints exactly why one real-linear isometric phase combination does not imply bi-circularity.

limitations: No complete corrected classification is given.
Only the stated dichotomy and the Form IV conclusion of arXiv:2609.18967v1 are assessed.
The elementary conjugation construction is not claimed to be historically new.
The full text of the 2019 corrigendum was not inspected.
Very recent or poorly indexed corrections or comments may not have been found.
Independent audit has not been performed.
